title: gate = classifier (vehicle / person / animal / none)
author: the operator
trigger: operator directive 2026-09-09 ~12:55: 'I don't see a reason for a gate or a pipeline cool down at this point. You can't know yet if the motion is from a vehicle, animal, or person / your logic flow does not mention the Yolo gate identifier. That should be next. Instead it says there's a cascade one and a cascade two? That totally doesn't make sense to me / After the Yolo gate identifies it as a vehicle, a person, or a animal, that's when we check if the pipeline cool down is in effect and if it is, that's when we stop the processing of that Web hook event'. Follow-up directive 2026-09-09 ~12:57: 'For 25b. If yolo classification is not vehicle, person, or animal, that flow gets dropped directly after the gate / Yes, and it should be logged as dropped.' The motivation: today's gate uses an opaque 'decision' field (Literal['vehicle', 'person', 'suppress']) that conflates 'YOLO saw a person' with 'YOLO saw a bench' with 'YOLO saw nothing'. The operator wants a single classification field -- if it isn't one of vehicle / person / animal, the pipeline drops the webhook before any cooldown check or Telegram dispatch happens. Currently the gate explicitly suppresses animals ('Rule 3: ANY crop high-conf animal -> suppress (no animal pipeline)') which means the system silently ignores the most common case at the farm: dogs walking the perimeter.
background: infra/gate.py today has DecisionType = Literal['vehicle', 'person', 'suppress']. _route_decision() at gate.py:644-715 returns (decision, class_label, confidence, reason). The 'suppress' outcome is overloaded: it triggers on (a) YOLO found nothing, (b) YOLO found an animal, (c) the timestamp / brightness rules said it was an artifact, (d) the AND intersection fell back to a raw-diff bbox. The operator wants to separate concern: the gate classifies; the pipeline routes. The 'animal -> suppress' rule at gate.py:692-694 needs to flip to 'animal -> return classification=animal'. The 'YOLO found nothing' case becomes classification=none. The 'timestamp/brightness artifact' case ALSO becomes classification=none (because YOLO did not actually classify anything). What DROPS the webhook is no longer the gate's suppress outcome -- the gate just reports; the pipeline drops on classification=none via PRD-V2-026.
shipping_definition: All US-025 stories marked done; pytest 150/150 (or higher) green; tree clean; infra/gate.py GateVerdict.decision is gone, replaced with classification: Literal['vehicle', 'person', 'animal', 'none']; _route_decision returns classification as a top-level field, not buried inside a decision tuple; _class_to_bucket helper exists in infra/quick_classifier.py and maps any yolo class_id to one of four values (vehicle / person / animal / none); the animal-suppression rule at gate.py:692-694 returns ('animal', ...) instead of ('suppress', ...); TD test for gate routing covers person + animal + suppression cases; integration test for the drop-after-gate behavior lives in PRD-V2-026, not here; no live Telegram dispatch during any of these tests.
scope_exclusions: Drop-after-gate pipeline change is NOT this PRD -- that is PRD-V2-026 US-026b. PRD-V2-025 only makes the gate emit classification; the listener's drop logic lives one PRD over.
Cooldown changes are NOT this PRD -- that is PRD-V2-026 entirely.
TG#1 / TG#2 / TG#3 changes are NOT this PRD -- that is PRD-V2-027.
Removing gate's legacy feature flags (GATE_KEEP_DISK_ARTIFACTS, MOTION_GATE_V2, NIGHT_SUPPRESS_ENABLED) is NOT this PRD -- V2-023 catalogued them; removal is a separate cleanup PRD.
Re-implementing YOLO inference is NOT this PRD -- infra/quick_classifier.py already does it. PRD-V2-025 only adds the bucket-mapping helper _class_to_bucket and consumes it.
Replacing DecisionType with a more abstract concept (a 'GateVerdict' protocol that everyone implements) is NOT this PRD -- keep the same GateVerdict dataclass, just rename fields.
Logging the dropped webhook is NOT this PRD -- that belongs in PRD-V2-026 US-026b where the drop happens.
design_principles: Gate classifies; pipeline routes. The gate emits `classification` and the pipeline decides what to do with `none`. This is the discipline that breaks the decision-overloading bug.

Classification is closed: 4 values, exactly. `vehicle` / `person` / `animal` / `none`. No `unknown`, no `unsure`, no `low_conf` -- those collapse to `none` because the gate cannot reliably route on them.

`none` does NOT mean 'YOLO was wrong' -- it means 'YOLO did not identify anything we can route on'. The gate logs the actual top_class + top_confidence at DEBUG so the operator can see what was actually on camera.
Animal is a first-class outcome. The 'no animal pipeline' reason that has lived at gate.py:692-694 for months is deleted -- this PRD is the day that reason dies.

_class_to_bucket uses infra/quick_classifier.py's existing PERSON_CLASSES / VEHICLE_CLASSES / ANIMAL_CLASSES sets. A class is in 'vehicle' if it's a member of VEHICLE_CLASSES (set membership is the truth), 'person' if PERSON_CLASSES, 'animal' if ANIMAL_CLASSES. Anything else returns 'none'. No optional strategy, no minimum-size overlap check -- set membership only.

DecisionType literal is replaced wholesale. No backward-compat alias. If a caller (test, script) is reading `gate_verdict.decision == 'suppress'`, that caller needs updating -- PRD-V2-025 is the migration moment.

Threshold edge: if top_confidence is below confidence_threshold (which the gate already computes), classification = none -- even if top_class is in PERSON_CLASSES. This is the operator's phrase 'you can't know yet' applied: low conf == unknown bucket.

No new env vars. No new feature flags. The bucket mapping is hardcoded in Python via sets that the operator owns. If the operator wants to add 'bicycle' to VEHICLE_CLASSES, they edit the source code -- not flip an env knob.

stories.title: add _class_to_bucket helper in infra/quick_classifier.py
acceptance: infra/quick_classifier.py exports _class_to_bucket(class_id: int) -> Literal['vehicle', 'person', 'animal', 'none'].
Implementation: if class_id in PERSON_CLASSES -> 'person'; elif class_id in VEHICLE_CLASSES -> 'vehicle'; elif class_id in ANIMAL_CLASSES -> 'animal'; else -> 'none'.
Function has a 4-line module-level docstring listing the mapping rule.

Test test_class_to_bucket.py exists with at least 6 cases: person (car -> 'none', but YOLO's 'person' class_id 0 -> 'person'), vehicle (YOLO car=2 -> 'vehicle'), animal (YOLO dog=16 -> 'animal'), unmapped (YOLO bench=14 -> 'none'), out-of-range (YOLO id=200 -> 'none').
Single commit: 'add _class_to_bucket helper (US-025a)'.

stories.title: flip DecisionType literal: add 'animal', keep 'none'
acceptance: infra/gate.py DecisionType literal changes from `Literal['vehicle', 'person', 'suppress']` to `Literal['vehicle', 'person', 'animal', 'none']`.

GateVerdict dataclass adds `classification: ClassificationType` (where ClassificationType = DecisionType) and `top_class: str` and `top_confidence: float` fields (top_class + top_confidence are the raw YOLO output for DEBUG logging).

GateVerdict.is_suppressed() method is REPLACED with GateVerdict.is_none() returning `self.classification == 'none'` -- the gate still needs a 'should I skip this' convenience check for the operator's mental model.

_route_decision() return signature is `(classification, top_class, top_confidence, reason)` -- no more `decision` field. The `decision` field on GateVerdict dataclass is GONE (not aliased, not deprecated -- deleted).

The animal-suppression rule at infra/gate.py:692-694 ('Rule 3: ANY crop high-conf animal -> suppress (no animal pipeline)') is DELETED. The replacement: any animal-crop outcome returns ('animal', 'dog', 0.85, 'animal_classified').
The 'timestamp / brightness artifact -> suppress' rule maps to ('none', <top_class>, <top_conf>, 'artifact').
The 'no YOLO detection -> suppress' rule maps to ('none', '', 0.0, 'no_detection').

tests/test_gate_routing.py updated: any test that asserted `decision == 'suppress'` now asserts `classification == 'none'`; any test that asserted decision == 'animal_suppressed' now asserts `classification == 'animal'`.
All test files in tests/ that reference gate_verdict.decision are updated. Grep verification: `decision` (the gate field) appears zero times in production code outside the literal type definition.
pytest tests/test_gate_routing.py -v 100% pass; pytest tests/ --ignore=tests/test_home_env.py still 150/150 (or higher) green.
Single commit: 'flip DecisionType to classification; add animal; remove 'suppress' overloading (US-025b)'.

stories.title: wired gate tests for the new classification field
acceptance: tests/test_gate_routing_classification.py exists with at least 5 cases: (a) YOLO sees a person at top_conf 0.85 -> classification == 'person', (b) YOLO sees a car at top_conf 0.91 -> classification == 'vehicle', (c) YOLO sees a dog at top_conf 0.78 -> classification == 'animal', (d) YOLO sees a bench at top_conf 0.92 -> classification == 'none', (e) YOLO finds nothing -> classification == 'none'.
Each test mocks the QuickClassifier dependency; no real YOLO or real llama-server calls.
pytest tests/test_gate_routing_classification.py -v 100% pass; full suite still green.
Single commit: 'tests for classification field (US-025c)'.

stories.title: log gate classification at INFO with top_class + top_confidence
acceptance: infra/gate.py's existing log.info() at the end of run_gate() prints classification + top_class + top_confidence + reason, replacing the old `decision=... class=... conf=...` line.
Log line is single-line, parsable, structured: `motion_gate: classification=animal top_class=dog top_confidence=0.78 reason=animal_classified`.
If classification == 'none', the log line still appears -- it is the operator's primary signal that YOLO found nothing.
Existing tests that grep the log line get updated.
Single commit: 'log classification field instead of decision (US-025d)'.
